Article Title: 'Power Banks' for satellites? Bengaluru Company builds tech to keep ageing spacecraft alive
Article Text:
Aule On-screen setup running multibody dynamics simulations and tracking system capturing hardware test data for position and velocity for correlation

Aule 2: Dark room hardware test setup where the team recreated on-orbit lighting conditions with a sun simulator and a target mounted on a robotic arm to simulate the target’s motion.

BENGALURU: What if satellites could simply plug into a power bank instead of drifting away when they run out of fuel? That’s the idea driving a Bengaluru startup building “jetpack” satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft, take over their propulsion duties and keep billion-dollar assets working years longer.After recently validating a key part of its technology at an Isro facility used for India’s SpaDeX docking mission, Aule Space is now preparing for what could become one of the world’s most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations.For satellite operators, running out of fuel doesn’t necessarily mean spacecraft have reached the end of life. In many cases, expensive communication satellites remain fully functional, but can no longer maintain their assigned orbital positions because they have exhausted the propellant needed for station-keeping. Once that happens, operators are forced to retire assets worth hundreds of millions of dollars.Aule has found another way. “We’re trying to build satellites which can go and dock to existing satellites in space which don’t have any installed ports... and extend their life so that they can keep generating revenue,” CEO Jay Panchal, told TOI. “It’s like a power bank,” he added.Instead of attempting the far more complicated task of refuelling satellites in orbit, Aule’s approach is to send a smaller “jetpack” spacecraft that docks with an existing communications satellite and assumes responsibility for station-keeping using its own propulsion system.The company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build and generate significant annual revenues.The challenge lies in docking with satellites that were never designed to be serviced. Rather than relying on dedicated docking ports, Aule will attach its spacecraft to the liquid apogee motor (LAM) nozzle, a standard external feature found on most geostationary satellites.If successful, the technology could help operators extract years of additional service from satellites that would otherwise become orbital relics. Panchal said each docked “jetpack” could extend a satellite’s operational life by up to 5 years.*Key Test Done*The startup recently completed a major milestone by testing its camera-based guidance, navigation and control system at the Rendezvous Simulation Laboratory (RSL) at Isro’s ISITE — the same lab where critical elements of the SpaDeX were validated.“We were the first non-govt entity to access RSL. This is the best kind of on-ground testing we can do for these capabilities,” Panchal said.One of Aule’s differentiators is its reliance on computer vision instead of multiple specialised sensors. Current docking systems typically use LiDAR, infrared cameras and other sensors. Aule says its spacecraft will perform the critical final approach using a single optical camera powered by onboard AI.The visual navigation models are trained using data generated in its own facilities and validated at Isro’s testbed before being deployed in orbit.The company is targeting an in-orbit demonstration next year, when it plans to launch two satellites that will autonomously dock in low-Earth orbit. Panchal claims it could be the world’s first private mission to perform non-cooperative docking in LEO using camera-only navigation. The mission will validate technologies that Aule ultimately intends to deploy around geostationary communication satellites.
Article Summary: Bengaluru startup building ‘jetpack’ satellites designed to latch onto ageing spacecraft. Aule space preparing for what could become one of the world’s most ambitious private satellite docking demonstrations. Company plans to target geostationary communication satellites, many of which cost more than $300 million to build.

Article Title: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles fast catching up with petrol ones
Article Text:
Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol-powered models in India, with CNG, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in July, just behind petrol’s 41.7%, according to data released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) Thursday. The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point, reflecting a rapid shift in buyer preferences.The trend came as India’s automobile retail market recorded its strongest-ever July performance, with overall registrations rising 25.8% year-on-year to a record 25.9 lakh units. For the first time, all six vehicle categories — two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, three-wheelers, tractors and wheeled construction equipment — posted their highest-ever July retail volumes, underscoring broad-based demand across the industry.Passenger vehicle retail sales increased 19% year-on-year to 4.1 lakh units, crossing the four-lakh mark for the first time in July. Within the segment, CNG vehicles accounted for 24.6% of sales, hybrids for 8% and electric vehicles for 7.9%. While hybrid vehicles continue to use petrol as their primary fuel source, automakers classify them as alternative-fuel vehicles because they combine an internal combustion engine with an electric powertrain to improve efficiency and reduce emissions.Petrol’s share, meanwhile, declined to 41.6% from 47.6% a year earlier. FADA said fresh model launches, affordability gains following GST changes and consumers’ increasing focus on lower running costs supported demand for alternative powertrains. The dealers’ body also noted that uncertainty surrounding the transition to E20 fuel appears to have nudged some buyers towards CNG, hybrid and EVs.The transition was equally evident in the two-wheeler market. Electric two-wheelers accounted for a record 11.2% of retail sales in July, up from 7.7% a year earlier.Overall EV retail registrations across all vehicle segments climbed to an all-time high of 3.28 lakh units during the month, taking EV penetration to about 12.7% of total vehicle retail sales from 9.6% a year ago. Maruti Suzuki retained its lead in the PV market in July, retailing over 1.6 lakh units.
Article Summary: Alternative-fuel passenger vehicles are on the verge of overtaking petrol-powered models in india. Cng, hybrid and electric vehicles accounting for 40.6% of passenger vehicle retail sales in july, just behind petrol’s 41.7%. The gap has narrowed sharply from 13.2 percentage points a year ago to just over a percentage point.

Article Title: Survey: 81% of study-abroad aspirants plan to return home
Article Text:
Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The foreign degree may be global, but the career plan is largely homeward-bound: 81% of Indian study-abroad aspirants surveyed by Oxford International said they planned to return to India after completing their courses. Nearly nine in 10 were the first in their family to pursue education overseas, while almost half said the decision to go abroad was their own.The findings are part of the third edition of Student Global Mobility Index, which combines 17,925 responses to core questions with about 2,400 responses to additional questions on courses, family background, information sources and post-study plans. Another 15% chose "applying for job" as their next step, without indicating whether the job would be in India or overseas.The biggest shift over three survey cycles is in who drives the decision. Self-motivated students rose from 29% in 2023-24 to 34% in 2024-25 and 49% in 2025-26. Family influence fell from 59% to 37% and then 36%. Younger students were more likely to rely on family guidance, while older applicants tended to decide independently. Self-motivation was highest in north and south India; family influence was strongest in the west and central region.Academic choices were heavily concentrated. Seven in 10 were applying for postgraduate courses, and 75% identified business and management as their main field. Health and medicine was a distant second at 8%. Sciences accounted for 2% and engineering 1%.Google searches led 39% of students to their institution, followed by agents (35%). But Google's lead widened on trust: 56% named it their most trusted source for education information, compared with 20% for college events and 9% for Instagram. AI tools were trusted most by 6% and YouTube by 5%.
Article Summary: Nearly nine in 10 were the first in their family to pursue education overseas. Almost half said the decision to go abroad was their own. Self-motivated students rose from 29% in 2023-24 to 34% in 2024-25. Family influence was strongest in the west and central region.

Article Title: CPRG launches Governance Dialogue series with focus on district-led development
Article Text:
The Centre for Policy Research and Governance (CPRG) on Thursday launched its Governance Dialogue series with a multi-stakeholder discussion on "District Led Development: Grassroots Stories, National Outcomes"

NEW DELHI: The Centre for Policy Research and Governance (CPRG) on Thursday launched its Governance Dialogue series with a multi-stakeholder discussion on "District Led Development: Grassroots Stories, National Outcomes", bringing together senior bureaucrats, policymakers, industry representatives, academics and media professionals to deliberate on strengthening governance through district-level administration.Addressing the inaugural session at the India International Centre, Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) vice chancellor prof. Badri Narayan stressed the need to bridge the gap between grassroots aspirations and policymaking."There is a real gap between how grassroots communities articulate their needs and how policy is conceptualised at the top, the language of the margins, the district and the policymaker are often very different, and what is needed is translation between them. That is precisely the gap platforms like CPRG can help bridge, by working from the bottom up," he said, adding: "Grassroots aspirations are changing rapidly, precisely because government schemes have succeeded in meeting basic necessities, and as development changes people's lives, it also changes what they aspire to next. The district is where this change must be understood, as it is not merely an administrative unit but a socio-cultural one, closest to the people at the margins."Delivering the keynote address, joint secretary in the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development, Parikipandla Narahari (IAS), said: "There is often a gap between people's felt needs and their real needs, and closing it is at the heart of good governance. More often than not, the disconnect lies not in policy itself but in implementation, how a policy is carried out on the ground is what matters most for a policymaker. Once implementation is strengthened at the district level, the policies we design naturally come closer to the people they are meant to serve."Major General K. Narayanan, programme director (Security and Strategic Affairs) at NITI Aayog, who attended as the chief guest, said: "The soul of India lives in its villages, and the district is our basic unit of governance. It is here that policy becomes people, budgets become schools, roads and hospitals, and governance acquires a humane face. For a developed India, policies cannot be made in Delhi alone, they must be shaped from Leh to Lakshadweep. Real innovation happens at the grassroots, and development at that level rests on a few simple principles: trust the district administration, celebrate innovation, measure outcomes rather than expenditure, and learn from one another, for diversity is our strength. In the end, development is about people, and even the smallest village or a single woman entrepreneur can be a force to be reckoned with."The first panel discussion featured Jalna District Collector Ashima Mittal, Indian Oil Corporation Executive Director (CSR) Bibhuti Ranjan Pradhan and The Economic Times Senior Editor Anubhuti Vishnoi. Panellists highlighted community participation in district development, the use of artificial intelligence in policymaking, and the need to move beyond infrastructure indicators towards quality-of-life outcomes.The second panel, comprising NTPC Executive Director (HR) Premlata, National Centre for Disease Control Deputy Director Dr. Avinash Sunthlia, CNN-News18 Senior Associate Editor Madhuparna Das and CPRG Senior Resident Fellow Banuchandra, discussed integrating government schemes, strengthening grassroots healthcare systems and promoting citizen participation in governance.CPRG said the Governance Dialogue series will continue in the coming months to foster sustained engagement among government, industry, academia and the media on public policy and governance issues.
Article Summary: The centre for policy research and governance (cprg) launched its governance dialogue series with a multi-stakeholder discussion on "district led development: grassroots stories, national outcomes" panellists highlighted community participation in district development, the use of artificial intelligence in policymaking.

Article Title: Govt tightens rules on AI-generated content, cuts removal deadline to 3 hours from 36 & mandates labels
Article Text:
The Centre has enacted or strengthened rules including IT Rules to curb AI‑generated deepfakes

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The government has tightened rules for social media platforms to tackle AI-generated deepfakes and other synthetically generated content, including fake audio, video and text.Under amendments to the IT Rules made in February, platforms must clearly label permissible AI-generated content and ensure it carries traceable metadata so users can identify “synthetically generated material”.The amended rules require platforms to take measures against unlawful AI-generated content, including deepfakes, child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate images and AI-based impersonation. Platforms must also inform users about the “legal consequences” of creating or sharing unlawful AI-generated content.The government has cut the deadline for platforms to remove unlawful content from 36 hours to 3 hours which shall start after receiving a valid notice from the government or a court. The rules also require intermediaries to deploy “reasonable and appropriate technical measures” to prevent users from creating or disseminating unlawful synthetic content.Significant social media intermediaries must use automated tools or other technical measures to proactively detect certain unlawful content, including material depicting rape or child sexual abuse. They must also make “reasonable efforts” to identify content that is identical to material previously removed.The government has also tightened grievance redressal timelines. Complaints involving sensitive issues such as nudity and impersonation must be addressed within 2 hours, compared with the earlier 24-hour timeline.Failure to comply with the IT Rules can result in platforms losing their safe-harbour protection under Section 79 of the IT Act, which protects intermediaries from liability for third-party content subject to certain conditions.The government said the measures are part of its efforts to ensure an “open, safe, trusted and accountable cyberspace” while promoting the “responsible development, deployment and adoption of AI” in India.
Article Summary: The centre has enacted or strengthened rules including it rules to curb ai‑generated deepfakes. The government has cut the deadline for platforms to remove unlawful content from 36 hours to 3 hours. Complaints involving sensitive issues such as nudity and impersonation must be addressed within 2 hours.

Article Title: IIT-G develops low-cost device to detect toxic metals, bacteria in water
Article Text:
IIT Guwahati researchers develop portable device that quickly detects toxic metals in water

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Researchers at IIT Guwahati have developed a portable optical sensing device that can quickly detect toxic metals, fluoride and bacteria in water samples, offering a low-cost tool for on-site water-quality checks in rural areas and places without easy access to laboratories.Named E-Eye, the device has detected arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride and Escherichia coli bacteria during laboratory tests, the institute said on Thursday. The estimated cost of the device is about Rs 3,500, with each sample test costing around Rs 2.The device uses a chemical reaction that produces a coloured compound. The intensity of the colour changes according to the concentration of the contaminant. E-Eye analyses the colour through optical sensing, converts the reading into digital data and displays the concentration of the toxicant.According to the researchers, the portable system can be deployed directly at water sources, unlike conventional testing equipment that generally requires samples to be taken to laboratories. It can also wirelessly transmit test results to water-treatment facilities.The team said E-Eye’s results were comparable with those obtained through standard UV-Visible and Atomic Absorption spectrophotometers.More than 2,700 samples have been tested using the device, it added.“The device operates on the Beer-Lambert law and combines optical sensing with digital electronics to generate accurate quantitative measurements. Our device has been able to successfully detect toxicants such as arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride, and Escherichia coli bacteria,” said Tapas K Mandal, professor in IIT Guwahati’s department of chemical engineering.The researchers said the device could support water-quality monitoring under the Centre’s Jal Jeevan Mission, which seeks to provide tap water to rural households while ensuring that the water supplied is safe.Apart from drinking water, E-Eye can be used to test environmental and biological samples, vegetables, food products, tea, herbal products, soil and milk, the institute said. It may also help industries monitor liquid effluents containing heavy metals, bacteria and odour-causing compounds.The research, supported by a grant from the ministry of electronics and information technology, has been published in the IEEE Sensors Journal. The team includes IIT Guwahati professors Mandal and Harshal B Nemade, along with researchers from the institute, KIIT Bhubaneswar and Ramakrishna Mission Residential College, Kolkata.The researchers have set up ENVIONIX Labs Pvt Ltd to commercialise the technology and are exploring an industry partnership for its transfer. They are also working to integrate solar panels and cloud connectivity into the device for remote monitoring and data management.
Article Summary: Iit guwahati researchers develop portable device that quickly detects toxic metals in water. The device has detected arsenic, lead, iron, chromium, fluoride and escherichia coli bacteria. The estimated cost of the device is about rs 3,500, with each sample test costing around rs 2.

Article Title: Govt backs 20 indigenous AI models, clears 58 centres of excellence
Article Text:
Eleven national-level hackathons and innovation challenges have so far resulted in 62 AI prototypes.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has selected 20 indigenous foundation-model proposals for support and sanctioned over 93 lakh hours of subsidised computing capacity as part of its effort to reduce India’s dependence on foreign artificial intelligence infrastructure and technologies.In a written reply in Lok Sabha on Wednesday, minister of state for electronics and information technology Jitin Prasada said the proposals were selected from 506 applications received under the IndiaAI Mission. They include 12 large multimodal models and eight small language models, with the intellectual property remaining with the developers.Among the models already launched are Sarvam AI’s 30-billion and 105-billion parameter models and Indus, Gnani.AI’s speech-to-speech model, BharatGen’s multilingual models and Avataar AI’s video-generation model.The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of Rs 10,371.92 crore over five years, is aimed at creating domestic capabilities in computing, foundation models, applications, research and responsible AI.The government has empanelled 15 computing service providers and approved subsidised computing support for 237 projects, involving 93.18 lakh GPU hours. It has also issued a purchase order for a high-performance AI computing system of around 1.1 exaflops at the National Informatics Centre’s data centre in Shastri Park, Delhi.Eleven national-level hackathons and innovation challenges have so far resulted in 62 AI prototypes, of which 20 have been deployed in public-sector institutions. The government has also approved 58 AI centres of excellence across states and Union territories. Of these, work has begun on 22 centres in 13 states and UTs.Another 13 projects have been selected to work on AI safety issues such as bias, privacy, algorithm audits, explainability and machine unlearning.Prasada said India was also strengthening the wider technology ecosystem through the National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems, which has an outlay of Rs 3,660 crore. Twenty-five technology innovation hubs have been established at academic institutions in areas including AI, robotics, cybersecurity, quantum technology and fintech.On semiconductors, the minister said 12 manufacturing projects involving committed investments of Rs 1.64 lakh crore had been approved under the Semicon India programme, with three having started commercial production.The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 on July 15 with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore. The programme will support Indian-designed chips, semiconductor fabrication and packaging units, and the production of materials, gases and equipment required by the industry.The government acknowledged that India’s AI computing ecosystem currently depends on imported graphics processing units procured through approved service providers. It said the IndiaAI and semiconductor missions were intended to progressively build domestic capabilities across the AI supply chain.Citing Stanford’s Global AI Vibrancy Report of November 2025, the reply said India ranked third globally in AI competitiveness and was the second-largest contributor to AI projects on GitHub.
Article Summary: The indiaai mission is aimed at creating domestic capabilities in computing, foundation models, applications, research and responsible ai. The government has empanelled 15 computing service providers and approved subsidised computing support for 237 projects. It has also issued a purchase order for a high-performance ai computing system.

Article Title: Josh Allen’s latest $1.7 million feat puts Bills superstar alongside Tom Brady and Patrick Mahomes in rare company
Article Text:
Josh Allen (Getty Images)

Why did Josh Allen's rookie card sell for a record $1.7 million?

What does this milestone say about Josh Allen's NFL legacy?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Josh Allen has added another milestone to his growing legacy, though this one came far from the football field. A one-of-one rookie trading card featuring the Buffalo Bills quarterback has sold privately for $1.7 million, according to Alt, setting a new record for an Allen card. The sale also places Allen alongside Tom Brady and Patrick Mahomes as the only NFL quarterbacks with multiple trading cards that have each sold for at least $1 million. While the achievement reflects Allen's soaring popularity among collectors, it also signals how strongly the hobby is betting on the next chapter of his career.The card that set the new benchmark is a 2018 Panini National Treasures Rookie Patch Autograph, numbered one of one. It features an NFL Shield patch from Allen's rookie season along with an autograph signed directly on the card, making it one of the rarest versions available from one of football's most sought-after product lines.Alt confirmed the private sale on August 6, with the final price eclipsing Allen's previous record by $350,000. That earlier mark had stood for less than three months after a one-of-one 2025 Topps Chrome NFL Honors Gold Shield autograph card sold for $1.35 million on May 22.The difference in value is not difficult to understand. Collectors often place greater importance on rookie-year cards because they represent the beginning of a player's professional journey. Add an on-card signature, an authentic NFL Shield patch and a one-of-one print run, and the result is a card many consider the ultimate version of Allen's rookie collectibles.According to Sports Illustrated's Conor B. McGrath, Brady, Mahomes and Allen are now the only NFL players to record multiple card sales worth at least $1 million. Brady has produced dozens of such sales over the years, while Allen and Mahomes each have two.The record sale carries a message beyond the trading card market. It shows that collectors are valuing Allen alongside two quarterbacks who have defined the modern NFL era.There is, however, one important distinction.Brady and Mahomes built their reputations through multiple Super Bowl victories. Allen, despite becoming one of the league's elite quarterbacks and helping turn Buffalo into a consistent contender, is still chasing his first Lombardi Trophy.That reality adds another layer to the $1.7 million purchase. The buyer is paying not only for what Allen has already achieved but also for what they believe he can still accomplish. At 30, his value is no longer based on untapped potential. Instead, it reflects confidence that his career will be remembered among the game's greats.A Super Bowl title would likely strengthen that belief and could push the value of his top collectibles even higher. Without one, comparisons with Brady and Mahomes will continue to invite questions because both already own championship legacies that cannot be debated.For now, though, Allen has reached a level that very few NFL players ever experience. His latest record was not tied to a new contract, an endorsement deal or another on-field accolade. It came from a single piece of memorabilia from his rookie season, and someone decided it was worth $1.7 million.
Article Summary: A one-of-one rookie trading card featuring josh allen has sold for $1.7 million. The sale places allen alongside tom brady and patrick mahomes as the only nfl quarterbacks with multiple trading cards that have each sold for at least $1 million.

Article Title: The untold story of how Cristiano Ronaldo built a garage worth $200m that even the ultra-rich quietly envy
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo's car collection (Instagram and Getty Images)

How many cars does Cristiano Ronaldo own?

What Bugattis does Cristiano Ronaldo own and how much are they worth?

Which Ferraris does Ronaldo have in his collection?

What other luxury cars does Ronaldo own apart from Bugatti and Ferrari?

Does Ronaldo actually drive all his cars or just collect them?

Why can't other billionaires just buy the same cars Ronaldo has?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two words. That is all Cristiano Ronaldo needed. "My toys," he captioned a recent Instagram post showing himself standing in a garage stacked with Ferraris, Bugattis, and machines that most people will only ever see in a screensaver. The post went viral within hours, and for good reason. What those photographs showed was not just an extraordinary collection of cars. They were a window into something far more telling about the man who built it -- one paycheck, one acquisition, one obsession at a time.Cristiano Ronaldo himself has admitted he has lost count. "If I had to bet, I'd say 40 or 41. I love Bugatti cars, they are completely different cars," he said in a past interview. That is not a brag. That is a man who genuinely cannot keep track of his own fleet -- which tells you most of what you need to know about the scale of what he has accumulated.His garage, depending on which estimate you trust, is valued at somewhere around $200 million. The collection spans Bugatti, Ferrari, McLaren, Lamborghini, Bentley, Rolls-Royce, Mercedes, and Porsche -- brands that most collectors would be proud to own even one of.Ronaldo owns several from each.This is where Cristiano Ronaldo's collection separates itself from every other celebrity garage on the planet. His Bugatti lineup includes a Veyron worth around £1.5 million, a Chiron worth £2 million, and the centrepiece -- a Bugatti Centodieci, one of only 10 ever built, priced at £7 million.Bugatti allocated all 10 Centodieci units before a single one left the factory floor. The waiting list was not public. You did not apply. Bugatti came to you, and only if your profile matched exactly what the brand wanted attached to that car. Ronaldo made that list. The secondary market value has climbed steadily since, making it as much a financial asset as a mechanical one.He reportedly also added a Bugatti Tourbillon -- the hybrid successor to the Chiron, priced at £3.2 million -- to the collection. If confirmed, Ronaldo now owns a private timeline of Bugatti's entire modern hypercar bloodline, from the Veyron era through to the present day. There are dedicated automotive collectors who have spent decades trying to build that exact sequence and still cannot match it.Cristiano Ronaldo's Ferrari stable is not made up of the models you see at a dealership. His reported lineup includes a Ferrari Monza SP2 worth £1.4 million, a Daytona SP3 worth £2 million, and a Purosangue -- Ferrari's first four-door, four-seat car, which still packs a naturally aspirated V12 because Ferrari does not do things quietly.The Monza and the Daytona both belong to Ferrari's Icona series -- a range of limited-production cars that the brand does not advertise publicly and does not sell to just anyone. Ferrari offers them directly to a curated list of its most long-standing, highest-spending clients. The Monza SP2 is a roofless tribute to Ferrari's 1950s racing barchettas. The Daytona SP3 is a V12-powered homage to the endurance racing cars that dominated Le Mans in the 1960s.For Ronaldo to own both tells you exactly how Ferrari classifies him as a customer. These are not cars you find by browsing. They find you.The fleet extends well beyond the two headline marques. Cristiano Ronaldo is also linked to a McLaren Senna at £750,000, a Lamborghini Aventador at £270,000, a Bentley Flying Spur at £250,000, and a Brabus-modified Mercedes-AMG G-Wagon at £600,000 -- a version so heavily customised that the original vehicle underneath is almost unrecognisable.Three Rolls-Royces sit somewhere in the collection too. His partner Georgina Rodriguez gifted him a Rolls-Royce Dawn -- the kind of present that most people would consider the centrepiece of their entire garage. For Ronaldo, it is one line in a much longer inventory.There is also reportedly a Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren tucked away in the fleet -- a car that caused genuine hysteria when it launched in the mid-2000s and now serves as a reminder of how far back Ronaldo's spending at this level actually goes. Al Nassr presented him with a BMW upon his arrival in Saudi Arabia, which his teammates also received. It is safe to assume it is not among his most-driven vehicles.Cristiano Ronaldo has addressed this directly. He has said in interviews that he views his car collection partly as an investment -- physical assets he acquires with an appreciation of their long-term value, not just their performance on the road.With 40-plus cars in rotation, driving each one even once a month would require a schedule more organised than most corporate calendars. Some cars are driven regularly. Others are stored, maintained, and allowed to appreciate quietly. The Centodieci, for example, is not a car most owners put serious road miles on -- its rarity and secondary market value make preservation the more logical choice.What makes that investment angle interesting is that it reframes the entire collection. This is not impulse spending scaled up to absurd levels. It is a deliberate accumulation of assets from marques whose most restricted models have historically held or increased their value. Ronaldo seems to understand the difference between buying a car and acquiring one.This is the part of Cristiano Ronaldo's garage that most coverage misses entirely. The cars are not just expensive. Several of them are effectively unbuyable -- not because of price, but because of access.Bugatti does not take open orders for cars like the Centodieci. The brand selects buyers based on their relationship history with the marque, their public profile, and their ability to represent the car appropriately. Ferrari's Icona programme works on similar principles. You need an established purchase history with the brand, a relationship with your regional Ferrari representative, and an invitation. Writing a cheque is the easy part. Getting the call is the hard part.Ronaldo's two decades at the summit of global sport have built him exactly the kind of profile both brands look for. His name carries weight in markets Ferrari and Bugatti care deeply about -- Europe, the Middle East, and Asia. He is, from a brand-alignment perspective, an ideal client. That is what separates his collection from someone who simply has enough money to spend. There are plenty of people with deeper pockets who do not have a Centodieci. Ronaldo does.
Article Summary: Cristiano ronaldo's garage is estimated to be worth around $200 million. The collection spans bugatti, ferrari, mclaren, lamborghini, bentley, rolls-royce, mercedes, and porsche. His bugatti lineup includes a veyron worth around £1.5 million. Cristiano ronaldo is linked to a mclaren senna at £750,000, a lamborghini aventador at £270,000 and a bentley flying spur at £250,000.

Article Title: Elon Musk is not pleased with Zohran Mamdani's grocery stores idea, calls him 'a thief and a liar, plain and simple'
Article Text:
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani

What Elon Musk said about Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan

What is Zohran Mamdani's grocery store plan

Critics question how New York will fund lower grocery prices

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has sharply criticised New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani over his plan to open city-backed grocery stores that promise to sell some everyday food items at prices below traditional retailers. Responding to a post on X (formerly Twitter) that questioned how the proposed stores would operate, Elon Musk dismissed the plan and accused Mamdani of misleading New Yorkers. “Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” Musk wrote in the post. The billionaire also argued that advances in AI and robotics, rather than government-backed programmes, would eventually make goods and services much cheaper or even free.Elon Musk made the comments while responding to an X post by user @jason, who criticised the economics behind Mamdani's proposal. The user argued that grocery businesses typically operate on very small profit margins and questioned the city's plan to seek private operators to run the stores.Responding to the post, Elon Musk wrote: “What they’re doing won’t matter.” He then suggested that AI and robots could eventually transform the cost of producing and delivering goods and services.“AI & robots will actually deliver the free goods & services that those thieves pretend to offer, while actually stealing from others,” Musk said.“Mamdani is a thief and a liar, plain and simple,” he added.Zohran Mamdani's administration has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of New York City's five boroughs. The city has allocated $70 million in capital funding for the programme. The first store is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in East Harlem, Brooklyn, Queens and Staten Island.Under the proposal, private grocery operators would handle day-to-day operations, including staffing, sourcing products and merchandising. The city would provide locations, cover major occupancy costs and set pricing and operating requirements.Mamdani's administration says shoppers could save about 30% on a core basket of groceries. It estimates that the programme could save an average New Yorker about $90 a month, or roughly $1,000 a year.The basket is expected to include fresh produce, meat and seafood as well as around 20 categories covering pantry staples, dairy and refrigerated products. Prices for these products would be locked monthly instead of changing week to week.The proposal has drawn criticism from economists, political commentators and business groups who question how the city can offer discounts of around 30% when grocery stores generally operate on thin profit margins. Critics argue that taxpayers could ultimately bear part of the cost through public funding, waived rent on government-owned properties and other support.They have also warned that publicly backed stores could put private supermarkets, bodegas and other small grocery businesses at a disadvantage because those businesses must pay expenses such as rent and property taxes themselves.Mamdani's administration, however, argues that removing some of those major operating costs is precisely what will allow the city-backed stores to offer lower prices. The plan comes as New Yorkers continue to face grocery prices that remain substantially higher than they were before the Covid-19 pandemic.
Article Summary: New york mayor zohran mamdani has proposed opening five city-backed grocery stores, with one planned for each of new york city's five boroughs. The first store is expected to open in hunts point in the bronx by the end of 2027, followed by locations in east harlem, brooklyn, queens and staten island.

Article Title: After 27 years and 18 desk moves, Jeff Dean is leaving Google; His ‘goodbye email’ explains why
Article Text:
Jeff Dean, Google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead AI startup Discovery Loop.

What Jeff Dean built at Google, and what he wants to build next

Jeff Dean's goodbye email to Google, in full

Subject: Thank you and farewell

Hi everyone,

It has been an absolute pleasure to work with you and to help build some of the most widely used and impactful products of all time. As a kid, I dreamed of helping build software that would be used by many people, and Google now has thirteen products used by more than a billion people (amazing!). Our work has had a tremendous impact in the world, and I have been lucky enough to collaborate and form friendships with many colleagues whom I deeply admire, respect, and enjoy.

It still brings me joy every time I see people out in the world using our products to find information, handle email, translate something, watch videos, learn new things, navigate and understand the physical world, browse the web, use their phone, run large-scale computations on our infrastructure, ride in an autonomous vehicle, or perform complex tasks with the help of our AI systems. I hope you all share this sense of joy, because it is a shared accomplishment!

My longtime friends and collaborators Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le and I have been excitedly discussing how AI can help discover new things with the right kinds of automated loops.

It's a big step, but we've decided to leave Google to co-found Discovery Loop, a new public benefit corporation whose mission is to automate machine learning, science, and engineering to accelerate discoveries and progress.

Ambitious as it sounds, we believe this approach can make meaningful progress against many of the NAE Grand Challenge problems (nae.edu/20782/grand-challenges-project), and we are excited about trying something new, in a smaller setting. Sundar and Alphabet have been very understanding and are helping to support us along with outside investors. We leave with the belief that Google and Gemini are extremely well positioned for amazing impact in the future and we will all be cheering you on from outside!

I have deeply enjoyed collaborating and starting many different kinds of projects here over the last 27 years, and I will miss many aspects of this. Some of the projects and memories I will cherish include:

Working on multiple generations of Google Search as we increased our index size 100X, our queries served / sec 1000X, and our update frequency for the index by 10,000X over a few-year period

Creating the first Google Ads system and later creating and launching Google Content Ads

Helping to launch Google News and Google Translate

Working on infrastructure like MapReduce, BigTable, Spanner, DistBelief, TensorFlow, and Pathways with an awesome set of people

Starting the TPU program and working on other exciting hardware projects with talented colleagues

Doing research with many others on unsupervised learning, model distillation, mixture-of-experts model architectures, word2vec, neural architecture search, RL for ASIC design, AI for health care, and working on multiple generations of Large Language Models (LLMs)

Seeing the awesome work that people in Google Brain and Google Research did over many years when I was lucky enough to manage these organizations

Starting the Gemini effort with Oriol Vinyals as co-tech-leads and working with an amazing team on multiple generations of Gemini and Gemma

Biking to offsites in Monterey

The "Run or Else…" group runs over the last few years

Changing offices 18 times, and visiting 29 Google offices across five continents (did you know that with a Google badge, you can make a cappuccino in more than 100 cities around the world?)

Most importantly, feeling lucky and inspired getting to work amongst such a wonderful and talented group of colleagues

To the many, many people with whom I have worked over the years, I apologize for this impersonal email rather than a face-to-face chat: I didn't want you all to find out through second- or third-hand gossip and it was impractical to tell everyone in a more personal way all at once.

I will be at Google through tomorrow, August 6th. If you're in Mountain View and are so inclined, please stop by my desk and say goodbye in person tomorrow, or drop me a reply to this email. There will be a [remainder redacted in the shared screenshot]

All the best!

-Jeff

Jeff Dean's farewell note to Google runs long, and the most telling part isn't about AI at all. It's a list. Wedged between scaling Google Search's index 100X and starting the TPU program, he mentions biking to offsites in Monterey, a group run called "Run or Else…", changing offices 18 times, and the fact that a Google badge gets you a cappuccino in more than 100 cities. Twenty-seven years, reduced to bullet points he clearly enjoyed writing.The news underneath the nostalgia: Thursday, August 6 is his last day. Dean, chief scientist at Google DeepMind and one of the very few engineers whose work touches nearly every layer of Google's stack, is leaving to co-found Discovery Loop, a public benefit corporation, with Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le. He joined in 1999, when the company had 25 employees. He leaves it at 190,000-plus.CEO Sundar Pichai 's send-off for Jeff Dean drew the same arc: over 27 years, he said, Dean and Ghemawat drove some of Google's most significant technology transitions, from its early search infrastructure to the neural networks that built the modern AI era. "On a personal note, it's been a privilege to work alongside Jeff and Sanjay," Pichai wrote, adding that Google will keep collaborating with the new startup as a founding investor and Cloud partner.Dean’s résumé is most of modern Google. He wrote the first Ads system, helped launch News and Translate, and with Ghemawat designed MapReduce, BigTable and Spanner—systems that became the template for how Amazon and Meta handled global traffic. The two are the only Google employees ever named senior fellow, the company's highest technical honour. Then came 2011 and Google Brain, the research lab Dean built that pushed the entire industry toward AI. Its early hires included Le and Vinyals, the same two men now following him out.That's the quiet irony here. Brain's researchers helped pioneer the technology behind today's chatbots, and Google was slow to act on it. After ChatGPT landed in late 2022, the company folded Brain into DeepMind, and Dean and Vinyals were put on Gemini. His profile inside Google appeared to shrink as Sergey Brin returned and took hold of the AI push.Discovery Loop is an attempt to skip the bureaucracy entirely. The four want to build AI that improves itself with little human input—recursive self-improvement—then point the same machinery at chip design, drug discovery and materials science. Dean's argument is that the experimental loop has always been human-intensive and doesn't have to be. Seed funding comes from Radical Ventures, Khosla Ventures and Alphabet itself, which has also agreed to supply compute for at least a year. It's structured as a public benefit corporation, like Anthropic and OpenAI, and Dean says it may make calls that aren't in the company's purest financial interests.The note ends with an apology for being an email. He didn't want people hearing it as second-hand gossip, he writes, and invites anyone in Mountain View to stop by his desk. That's the tell. A man who spent 27 years building systems for a billion users at a time signed off worrying about how a few thousand colleagues would find out.
Article Summary: Jeff dean, google's 30th employee and chief scientist, is leaving after 27 years to lead ai startup discovery loop. Dean: "it has been an absolute pleasure to work with you and to help build some of the most widely used and impactful products of all time" jeff dean, chief scientist at google deepmind, is leaving to co-found discovery loop.

Article Title: After telling employees to stop using Claude Code, Microsoft's internal memo has more 'bad news' for Anthropic
Article Text:
Microsoft's new internal memo makes OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default model for its engineers, replacing a setup that had been quietly routing GitHub Copilot work to Anthropic's Claude.

GitHub Copilot's auto-router was quietly sending Microsoft engineers to Claude

Microsoft's AI token budget targets now put a ceiling on every division

Anthropic keeps its Microsoft deals but loses the GitHub Copilot default

Microsoft spent May telling its Windows, Office and Surface engineers to wind down Claude Code and move to GitHub Copilot CLI before the fiscal year closed on June 30. That looked like a licensing decision, and an expensive one for Anthropic. This week's internal memo suggests the harder blow was still coming.Jay Parikh, the executive vice president who runs Microsoft's CoreAI organisation, wrote to his teams that "tokenmaxxing is not what we are optimizing for," asked engineers to review their own AI spending, and made OpenAI's GPT-5.6 the default model for internal use. 404 Media first reported the memo, which lands at a company that has just posted another record quarter and is still worried enough about its own AI bill to put a ceiling on it.The default-model line is the part Anthropic will feel. According to reporting by Alex Heath, Microsoft's internal GitHub Copilot configuration previously ran on an auto-router that leaned mostly on Anthropic's models. In practice, thousands of Microsoft engineers were writing code with Claude tokens without ever choosing Claude, and Microsoft was paying for it. Cancelling Claude Code took away a product people had asked for.Changing the router takes away the traffic nobody had to ask for.Parikh framed it as efficiency rather than divorce. Shifting more workloads to OpenAI models, he wrote, helps the company get greater value from its token investment. He also stressed that Microsoft is not chasing lower usage: "We are not optimizing for fewer tokens. We are optimizing for more impact per token."Since July, every Microsoft division has carried an AI token budget target, and employees can look up their individual spend on an internal dashboard. The guidelines seen by 404 Media note that many engineers were burning through anywhere from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars in tokens each month.Microsoft is late to this. Uber's engineering organisation exhausted its entire planned 2026 AI coding budget in four months. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella himself admitted at a live Hard Fork taping in June that plenty of tokenmaxxing was happening inside Microsoft, called the habit addictive, then delivered the line that now reads like policy: don't use frontier models for non-frontier problems.None of this ends the relationship. Claude models remain reachable through Copilot CLI, Microsoft Foundry customers still get Sonnet, Opus and Haiku under the November deal, and Microsoft has continued to favour Anthropic inside Microsoft 365 Copilot for tasks where it outperforms OpenAI. Microsoft even worked with Anthropic to bring Claude Cowork technology into Microsoft 365 Copilot.But defaults are where volume lives. Anthropic's business has been built substantially on enterprise coding workloads, and its largest customer just rewired its internal plumbing to send those workloads elsewhere by default. Rajesh Jha's May memo said Copilot CLI gave Microsoft a product it could shape directly with GitHub. Parikh's memo explains the other half of that sentence. Microsoft wanted a tool it controlled, and a bill it could predict, and Claude was expensive on both counts.
Article Summary: Microsoft makes openai's gpt-5.6 the default model for its engineers. The company had been quietly routing github copilot work to anthropic's claude. Microsoft ceo satya nadella admitted at a live hard fork taping that plenty of tokenmaxxing was happening inside microsoft.

Article Title: Twitter product head resigns, sends thanks note to Elon Musk and team; Tesla CEO responds
Article Text:
Nikita Bier thanked Elon Musk and team



Tesla CEO Elon Musk responds to Nikita Bier’s post



Read Nikita Bier’s complete post here



Ladies and gentlemen, it's time to pass the torch and demote myself to my natural state: a poster. I'll be stepping back from leading product for 𝕏 and will continue on as an advisor.

Serving the X community has been the privilege of a lifetime. X is, and will remain, the most important communication technology in history. But running this app is a 24/7 job and it's now time for me to take a breather.

The app is seeing unprecedented growth in new users & engagement. We continue to break records every month. We've climbed 70 spots in the App Store since this time last year.

Nikita Bier, the product head at X (formerly known as Twitter) has stepped down from his position after serving in the role for just over a year. Bier announced his decision in a post shared on X, saying it was ‘time to pass the torch and demote myself to my natural state: a poster. ’ He added that he will continue to advise the company. Bier, a serial entrepreneur and Lightspeed venture partner, took over the product lead role in July 2025. In his farewell note, he highlighted overseeing the launch of nearly 30 new products and rebuilding core aspects of X, including the timeline, Android app, onboarding, notifications, and chat. He also pointed to record-breaking growth in users and engagement, noting X had climbed 70 spots in the App Store over the past year.His tenure also coincided with controversies, including issues with Grok, the chatbot developed by Musk’s xAI, which was misused to generate harmful content. Despite these challenges, Bier emphasized that X remains “the most important communication technology in history,” but said running the app was a 24/7 job and he needed a breather.Bier expressed gratitude to Elon Musk and the X team, writing: “Serving the X community has been the privilege of a lifetime… None of this would have been possible without the incredible team here.” He named colleagues who will continue leading design, product engineering, and mobile engineering. Musk responded to Bier’s post, thanking him for his contributions.Responding to the goodbye note shared by Bier on X, Tesla CEO Elon Musk thanked him for his contribution. “Thanks for helping make this platform much better! You will be missed,” wrote Musk.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
